articles.title: Team identifies an evolutionarily conserved enhancer that regulates tendon and ligament development
articles.source: Phys.org - latest science and technology news stories
articles.summary: A research team has uncovered fundamental molecular mechanisms governing the formation of tendons and ligaments, which are essential for musculoskeletal integration. Understanding these mechanisms could pave the way for the regeneration of tendons, ligaments and their attachment sites, known as entheses, which have limited capacity for functional repair after injury because of their poor vascularization.

articles.title: Scientists may have found a shortcut to calorie restriction’s anti-aging benefits
articles.summary: Moderate calorie restriction lowered an immune protein called C3 that appears to help drive chronic inflammation as the body ages. Blocking the same protein reduced age related inflammation in mice, raising the possibility that future treatments could mimic some benefits of calorie restriction without severe dieting.

articles.title: 190-year-old DNA reveals a hidden pangolin species
articles.summary: DNA from a nearly 190-year-old museum specimen has helped scientists confirm a distinct Himalayan pangolin species hiding in plain sight in Nepal and northern India. The discovery could give conservationists a powerful new way to trace illegally traded pangolin scales back to the species and regions being targeted by poachers.

articles.title: Manhattan-sized ice island breaks off Greenland’s Petermann Glacier
articles.summary: A Manhattan-sized ice island has broken away from Greenland’s Petermann Glacier after years of growing fractures weakened its floating ice tongue. Scientists expect two more huge sections could soon detach, potentially removing about 22 percent of the remaining ice tongue.
